still_true: Wegovy's US list price is still $1,349 a month, and almost nobody pays it.
The FDA has approved no generic semaglutide or tirzepatide in the US; generic liraglutide is still the only generic incretin on the US market.
The TrumpRx cash channel still operates, and oral Wegovy starting doses still cost $149 a month there.

Congress has not reopened the ~$41B CBO-scored permanent benefit, and Medicare still pays for no incretin prescribed for weight loss alone. Every Medicare dollar still runs through a non-weight indication.

The September 2027 tri-agency guidance allowing up to 30% premium differentials tied to verified adherence still stands, and Illinois's ban on adherence-conditioned premiums is still the only state ban in force.

population.note: FICTIONAL. Cycling arithmetic: 40.4% ever-used − 29.3% current = 11.1% of adults who used and are off now. About 54% of current users are on a second or later course (15.8 points), and 3.0 points cycled and are off again, so (15.8 + 3.0) / 40.4 ≈ 46.5% of ever-users have cycled. The other 8.1 points stopped once and have not restarted. This is consistent with the parent's persistence figures (one-year persistence ~one-third on self-administered products, ~60% in clinic and conditioned tracks, and ~80% for Medicare dementia-label users in their first year, who face low copays and a 'protect your memory' framing). Planned 'drug holidays' of 1–3 weeks count as continuous use, not as stopping. Age check: 0.20×16.5 + 0.33×28.5 + 0.24×40 + 0.23×30.5 = 3.3 + 9.4 + 9.6 + 7.0 ≈ 29.3. Income thirds (34/30/24) average ~29.3. Users: 29.3% of ~276M adults ≈ 80.9M. FICTIONAL payer mix: Medicare ~20.5M (25.3%); Medicaid ~6.8M (8.4%); TRICARE/VA ~1.6M (2.0%; ~0.25M active duty, ~0.8M non-active-duty TRICARE, ~0.55M VA; TRICARE-for-Life users are counted in Medicare); commercial ~18.0M (22.2%, of which ~10.3M are in conditioned tracks); legitimate cash ~28.0M (34.6%, including ~2.6M on calm/focus plans and ~6.3M who stay indefinitely on the $149 starting dose); imported or counterfeit ~6.0M (7.4%). Sum: 20.5 + 6.8 + 1.6 + 18.0 + 28.0 + 6.0 = 80.9. Public programmes together (28.9M, 35.7%) are now the largest payer channel, just ahead of cash (28.0M). 65+ users ≈ 0.23×276M×30.5% ≈ 19.4M, ~18.5M of them through Medicare. Medicare's other ~2M are disability enrollees under 65. The bottom third rose 17.5 → 24, the largest gain of any third, because the new coverage is public: Medicaid AUD (~1.8M), dementia-label coverage for duals and Medicaid 60–64s, and low-income-subsidy Part D copays. About 19% of adults have obesity and have never used a drug, now concentrated in uninsured 30–59-year-olds in non-expansion Southern states. Their age group misses the new public routes. Pediatric: 2.1% of under-18s are on a drug, ~3.9% of 12–17s and ~0.8% of 6–11s. About 62% of new 6–11 starts are Medicaid/CHIP. About 5.8M children live with a parent who regained after stopping. About 6.1M adults have now used an incretin continuously for 5+ years, the population exposed to the new hypodipsia signal.

access.public_coverage: FICTIONAL. Medicare (~20.5M users) still pays only through diabetes, CV, CKD, OSA, AUD and dementia-risk codes, all behind PA. Since the Nov 2035 approval, the dementia route covers tirzepatide in adults 60+ with BMI ≥27 without established CVD. That made Part D the default payer for older Americans without any statute. Arithmetic: 20.5M × ~$236 average net/month × 12 ≈ $58.1B gross Part D incretin spend, up from ~$38.3B. Net price per fill is flat, so the rise is all volume and mix. Dementia route: ~6.9M × $250 × 12 ≈ $20.7B; ~1.9M of those 6.9M were cash 'dementia-prevention' payers who moved onto Part D. AUD route: ~1.3M × $205 × 12 ≈ $3.2B. The 2036 Part D base beneficiary premium rose ~9%, the largest rise since the 2025 redesign. Medicaid (~6.8M): 4.4M + 0.9M AUD growth + 0.6M dementia-label 60–64s (a covered outpatient use, so states cannot exclude it) + 0.9M diabetes/CV/pediatric growth = 6.8M. 6.8M × ~$190 net × 12 ≈ $15.5B. Seven states still cover adult weight-loss use. The NDAA FY2036 Metabolic Readiness authority lets military treatment facilities prescribe for body-composition failure without a weight-loss exclusion.
access.generic_rest_of_world: Indian generic semaglutide is still $4–30 a month in India and 100+ export markets. Chinese tirzepatide and retatrutide-analogue vials are $20–70 where patents are not enforced. Delivered to US addresses under the unchanged Section 232 tariff and Indian export-licence regime, they cost ~$90–190. Canadian and Brazilian generic semaglutide is CAD 45–80 and BRL 160–280. India and China still supply roughly two-thirds of world incretin volume.
access.note: FICTIONAL. Prices stalled. Lilly and Novo made no cash cuts in 2035 or 2036, the first two flat years since 2026. US branded net prices were flat in 2035 and up ~1% in 2036. Three things stopped the drift: Medicare dementia-label volume, the allocated launch of retatrutide 12 mg, and litigation reserves. Cash prices: TrumpRx Wegovy pill $149 starting and $199 maintenance (unchanged); Foundayo $149–229; Wegovy/Zepbound injectables $249–299; MariTide $249; oral amycretin ~$449 with no TrumpRx price; retatrutide (24% dose) $399. Retatrutide 12 mg has a $1,499 list price and $549 cash direct, under allocation with a 6–10 week LillyDirect waitlist. Business Group on Health (Nov 2036): 35% of employers cover weight management, and ~two-thirds condition it. Conditioned tracks hold ~10.3M. About 40% of tracks now allow two 'declared holidays' a year, logged in advance, without losing the premium tier. Gray market ~6.0M, with the growth in 'reta' vials sold to people waiting on the Lilly list. Orals are ~56% of users.

on_market_classes: GIP/GLP-1 dual agonist, weekly injectable (tirzepatide: Zepbound/Mounjaro)
GIP/GLP-1/glucagon triple agonist, weekly injectable (retatrutide, standard dose and 12 mg high dose approved Feb 2036)
GLP-1/amylin unimolecular co-agonist, daily oral (oral amycretin)
GLP-1 agonist/GIP-receptor antagonist antibody conjugate, monthly injectable (maridebart cafraglutide: MariTide)
GLP-1 agonist, daily oral peptide (Wegovy pill 25 mg; Rybelsus)
GLP-1 agonist, daily injectable (liraglutide: Saxenda, incl. generics)
Activin type II receptor antibody muscle adjunct (bimagrumab, restricted label)
indications_beyond_weight_and_diabetes: moderate-to-severe alcohol use disorder (oral semaglutide / Wegovy pill). The 2035 VA/DoD guideline lists it first-line with naltrexone and acamprosate, and ASAM and APA list it as an option
pediatric obesity ages 6–11 (liraglutide incl. generics; weekly semaglutide), with growth and eating-disorder monitoring

reduction of risk of all-cause dementia in adults with obesity and established CVD, extended Nov 2035 to adults 60+ with BMI ≥27 without CVD (tirzepatide). Baseline DXA is required for women 65+, and the label carries a hip-fracture warning for women 70+
mainstream_offlabel_uses: 'calm' and 'focus' low-dose plans via telehealth (~2.6M subscribers), with fewer AUD-label scripts after CMS audit recoupments
planned 'drug holidays': skipping 1–3 weekly doses or pausing the pill for weddings, holidays, tasting trips or to 'feel things again'
patient-led down-titration below label maintenance doses to manage flatness
dementia-prevention use by 50–59-year-olds, cash-paid, outside the new 60+ label
indefinite use of the $149 TrumpRx starting dose as maintenance (~6.3M)
semaglutide in 12–14-year-olds at doses above label titration in gray channels
drugs.pipeline_note: FICTIONAL. Lilly filed the retatrutide 12 mg sNDA in Jan 2035 on TRIUMPH extension data showing ~29.5% mean weight loss at 80 weeks. FDA approved it in Feb 2036 (13 months), with anhedonia and dysaesthesia listed among adverse reactions. This realises the ~30% triple-agonist driver as a higher-dose form of an existing product. No new molecule was eligible. Fill-finish capacity limits supply until Lilly's Concord and Lebanon (IN) lines reach full output in 2037. Lilly resubmitted the tirzepatide dementia extension in Jan 2035, and FDA approved it for 60+ in Nov 2035 with fracture language. Oral semaglutide AUD remains the only AUD label. Lilly filed orforglipron for AUD in Jun 2036, and the earliest approval is mid-2037. High-dose injectable amycretin is in phase 3 and has not been filed. Implants remain in phase 2 and are not on the market. The global incretin market is ~$235B (2035).

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the leading cause of discontinuation outside clinic tracks. Retatrutide 12 mg titration nausea runs ~45%. Holiday restarts at full dose without re-titration cause a recognisable wave of ED visits for vomiting.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled. In 2035 labels added re-titration guidance after missed doses.

safety_ledger.effect: Gastroparesis, ileus and bowel obstruction (persistent delayed gastric emptying)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: The first two MDL gastroparesis bellwethers (Oct 2035, Mar 2036) split: a defence verdict for Lilly and a $14M plaintiff verdict against Novo, now on appeal. GI claims are ~44,000. Persistence after stopping is still disputed in cohort data.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: No new labelling. More bellwethers are scheduled for 2037.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Elevated with rapid weight loss. Retatrutide 12 mg users show the highest cholecystectomy rates in the class.
Still no causal confirmation; absolute risk low. Plaintiffs still plead it together with EPI.

safety_ledger.effect: Lean mass (muscle) loss and bone-density loss
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Medicare hip-fracture HR is ~1.3 after more than 2 years and ~1.45 after three or more cycles. The new 60+ dementia-label population is the largest exposed group yet, mostly older women. Bimagrumab users are ~310k.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Hip-fracture warning for women 70+ and baseline DXA requirement on the tirzepatide dementia label. Part D plans fold bimagrumab into the same PA bundle.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Conflicting cohorts; absolute risk very low.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Listed in adverse reactions; no class warning.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: No new adult signal, including on retatrutide 12 mg and AUD-label users. The pediatric psychiatric concern remains restrictive eating.

safety_ledger.effect: Reward blunting / emotional flattening ('Ozempic personality', anhedonia)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: An FDA Sentinel low-dose analysis (Sep 2035) found clinically meaningful anhedonia in ~5% of calm-plan-dose users vs ~3.5% of controls, ~7% on maintenance doses and ~13% on retatrutide 12 mg. The effect is dose-related and mostly resolves within 3–6 weeks of stopping or down-titrating. That finding is what made holidays common practice.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Anhedonia is listed in adverse reactions on the retatrutide 12 mg label. Class labels carry no boxed warning and no change.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Half to two-thirds regain within 18 months, worse after repeated cycles. Short holidays of 1–3 weeks produce ~1–2 kg rebounds that mostly reverse. Delta regain from the 2033 tariff is now chronic.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: None directly; it underpins conditioned coverage.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: B12, iron, vitamin D and thiamine deficiency (the last in AUD-label users who keep drinking), and low ferritin in adolescent girls. Protein shortfall in 70+ dementia-label users is now a geriatric clinic staple.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Annual micronutrient panel language retained; dietitian referral added to the dementia-label medication guide.

safety_ledger.effect: Exocrine pancreatic insufficiency after 5+ years of continuous use
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: EPI incidence is ~2× after 5+ years on semaglutide and ~1.3× on tirzepatide. EPI claims are ~61,000. Novo's reserve was raised to ~$7.4B. No global settlement.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: The DOJ civil investigative demand is still open. FDA closed out Novo's Form 483 in 2035 after a pharmacovigilance remediation plan.

safety_ledger.effect: Chronic hypodipsia (reduced thirst) with kidney stones and heat-related illness after 5+ years of continuous use
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Novel and not predicted by trials, and no excess appears in the first 3 years. A Danish registry and VA Million Veteran Program cohort (Jul 2035) found nephrolithiasis HR ~1.5 and hospitalised hypernatraemia or heat illness HR ~1.6 in users with 5+ years of continuous exposure (~3.0 vs ~1.9 per 1,000 person-years in 65+). The effect is class-wide and larger with tirzepatide and retatrutide. The leading hypothesis is central adaptation of GLP-1R signalling in thirst circuits. In the Aug 2035 Phoenix heat wave, Maricopa County flagged ~140 heat admissions in long-term users. In Jun–Jul 2036, Army heat-casualty reviews at Fort Moore and Fort Bragg found incretin use in 11 of 63 NCO heat injuries.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA Drug Safety Communication (Mar 2036): scheduled-hydration counselling and summer sodium/renal checks for 65+ long-term users. A postmarketing study is required. No label restriction. Army TB MED 507 was updated with a hydration protocol for users.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon effects beyond ~5 years; effects in children on drug for decades; effects of repeated on/off cycling
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: About fourteen years of semaglutide follow-up exist. Hypodipsia shows the long tail is real and not limited to the pancreas. Holiday cycling, as distinct from stopping, is uncharacterised. There are still no data on indefinite starting-dose use.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Pediatric bone and growth PMRs continue. FDA asked sponsors for 10-year pooled renal and electrolyte data.

safety_ledger.effect: Compounded / counterfeit / imported product harms (dosing errors, contamination, substitution)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Adverse-event reports tied to non-approved product passed ~36,000. 'Reta' vials sold to Lilly-waitlist buyers are the growth line. A second re-filled-vial infection cluster hit Alabama in 2035 (~90 cases, 1 death).
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: The Section 232 tariff and India export checks are unchanged. CDC issued a health advisory. No new statute and no state action.

safety_ledger.effect: Growth deceleration, delayed puberty and restrictive eating in children started young
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Height velocity is still ~0.5–0.6 cm/year below expected in prepubertal starters on liraglutide and semaglutide, with partial catch-up after stopping. The Swedish ARFID HR is ~1.8. The first liraglutide 6–11 starters reach puberty with no final-height data.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Monitoring language and medication guide unchanged. The AAP is still lifestyle-first for prepubertal children. No REMS.

safety_ledger.effect: Alcohol-related harms on the AUD label (dehydration, alcoholic ketoacidosis, aspiration with vomiting during binge drinking)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: ~1 per 2,000 person-years in the PMR's first readout. Overlaps with hypodipsia in long-term users who binge in heat. VA reports holiday binges ('pill off, bottle on') as a pattern.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Label counselling on titration and hydration. The VA/DoD guideline advises against holidays for AUD patients.

food_and_beverage.state: About 47% of households have a user. Snack and confectionery volumes are ~15–17% below 2025 and sugary drinks ~13%. Dollar sales are flat to slightly down. The new 65+ wave on the dementia label is hitting categories that had held up, such as ice cream, cookies and premium sweet baked goods. Publix and Winn-Dixie stores in Florida's retirement corridors cut freezer-aisle dessert space and added oral rehydration and electrolyte bays after the March 2036 FDA communication. Electrolyte drinks are the fastest-growing beverage line. The Delta 'tariff bounce' persists.

alcohol.state: US spirits volumes are ~21% below 2025, beer ~13% and wine ~14%. Wine is new to the list: its 55+ core is now on dementia-label tirzepatide. Sonoma and Lodi growers report non-renewal of ~9% of grape contracts for 2036. Bardstown and Louisville distillers cut another ~1,200 jobs. VA/DoD first-line AUD guidance emptied base-adjacent bars around Fort Bragg and Killeen. Non-alcoholic and 'calm' lines are ~6% of category dollars. Holiday-weekend drinking spikes are a visible pattern in distributor data.

restaurants.state: Traffic is flat and average checks are slightly up, because prices rose faster than portions shrank. In The Villages, Sun City and Scottsdale, early-dinner chains run 'half plates' and drop all-you-can-eat. Cruise lines cut buffet square footage. Late-night bar revenue in Midwestern mid-sized cities has stabilised at its new low. Some steakhouses market 'holiday dinners' to people timing a skipped dose.

apparel.state: Plus-size specialists keep shrinking, and retatrutide 12 mg users drive a market for alteration and loose skin-compression garments. Resale serves cyclers. Mature-women's brands see size-down demand for the first time.

fitness.state: Strength training keeps growing. Senior resistance programmes billed through Medicare Advantage supplemental benefits grew after the dementia label and DXA requirement. Military body-composition clinics contract with budget chains near bases. InBody scans remain a track requirement.

insurance.state: Pharmacy trend is ~+8% because net prices stopped falling and retatrutide 12 mg PA requests are heavy. Employer coverage is 35% and mostly conditioned. Trackers now bill a 'declared holiday' feature. The 2036 Part D base premium rose ~9%. Medicare Advantage plans compete on low-copay dementia tiers. CMS's AUD coding audit recouped ~$310M from two telehealth platforms for unsupported diagnoses. Medicaid absorbed ~$15.5B of incretin spend without a single state vote.

pharma.state: Growth is supply-constrained. Lilly is capacity-bound on retatrutide 12 mg and gaining Medicare share through the dementia label. Novo grows on oral amycretin while carrying a ~$7.4B reserve. Neither cut prices, and analysts call 2035–36 'the plateau'. Electrolyte and renal-monitoring makers benefit from the hypodipsia communication. Indian exporters keep redirecting to the Gulf, Latin America and Africa.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: Being on the drug no longer signals anything. Being off does, and it needs explaining: pregnant, between courses, priced out, a holiday, or 'my pancreas'. Beyond that, the body still reads as payer. Lifted and scanned means a track. Retatrutide-gaunt with loose skin means $549 cash and a waitlist. Slow-thin on the starting dose means TrumpRx. A 72-year-old carrying a 40-ounce bottle with a sip alarm is on Part D's dementia tier. A soldier's tape-test result now has a prescription field.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: Muscle remains the class uniform. Among upper-income 30–50s the elite boast has shifted from 'off-drug lean' to 'I take holidays and nothing happens'. Medicare made the drug ordinary for retirees regardless of income, and the bottom third gained faster than anyone through public programmes. Uninsured working-age Southerners in non-expansion states, outside every public route, are now the visibly larger population. Upper-income parents still refuse the drug for prepubertal children.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Meals are shorter and smaller, and that is no longer remarked on. The new ritual is the holiday meal: families plan Thanksgiving, weddings and bar mitzvahs around who is pausing, and caterers ask about it on RSVP forms. In The Villages, potlucks went to tasting portions. Bread Alone (~1,100 congregations) keeps holding 'full table' suppers, now attended partly by people on a holiday.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: App tags shifted from 'on' to 'off' and 'holiday-friendly'. Being off is now the disclosure. People time first dates and anniversaries to a skipped dose, and some couples synchronise holidays. 'Flat' became ordinary vocabulary for a partner who is not present.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: Appetite is treated as a setting. People talk about dialling it down, taking a week off from the drug, or titrating for a trip. In the Delta, 'the hunger tax' persists as a political phrase. The 2034 backlash coalition fragmented after normalisation. MAHA groups now focus on the pediatric label and hypodipsia in seniors, and Unmuted rebranded as a holiday-advocacy group pushing employers to allow pauses.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Sentinel puts clinically meaningful anhedonia at ~5% at calm-plan doses, ~7% at maintenance and ~13% on retatrutide 12 mg, vs ~3.5% in controls. With ~80.9M users, roughly 5M people meet the clinical threshold, and far more describe sub-threshold flatness. A Pew survey (Mar 2036) finds ~38% of current users took at least one planned holiday in the past year, and ~22% have self-down-titrated. Calm/focus subscribers are ~2.6M, and fewer of them are on the AUD label (~24%, down from ~35%) after the audit recoupments.
interior_life.framing: The public frame shifted from feature to complaint. 'Flatness' is now an ordinary side effect, like nausea, managed by dosing and holidays. Platforms still sell 'quiet', but they now also sell holiday scheduling. Clinicians call it dose-related reward blunting with reversible offset. The Army calls it 'affect monitoring'.
interior_life.effect_on_work: About 10.3M employees are in conditioned tracks. Undeclared holidays still cost the premium tier, and 'holiday quota' became a bargaining item in the 2036 UAW and Teamsters contracts. The NDAA Metabolic Readiness programme forbids holidays for enrolled soldiers. Commanders see adherence flags in MEDPROS, and the summer heat-injury reviews put that rule under question. ~40 large police departments fund the drug for officers through wellness grants, and some unions resist the adherence data. FMCSA is still silent on calm plans.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: 'Flat' is a critical term: reviewers in Pitchfork and the Times describe 'post-pill' albums and novels as affectless or serene. A 2035 Kacey-Musgraves-style hit called 'Holiday Week' became a karaoke standard. Comedy shifted from 'dry' sets to holiday material. Live music in Columbus and Louisville stays thin, though venues book 'holiday weekend' shows. Sportsbooks see handle spike on long weekends.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Couples therapists now treat 'mismatched holidays' as a standard presentation: one partner pauses to feel more and the other does not. Pill-window mornings persist. Some couples plan conception and anniversaries around synchronised pauses. Retirees on the new label report the flatness complaints younger users had in 2030.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: Normalisation took the edge off the backlash. In the 2036 campaign, candidates' use disclosures drew no headlines, and nobody claims anymore that users are a sedated bloc. The live political fights are the Part D premium rise in a stalled-price market, hypodipsia among seniors, the soldiers' no-holiday rule, and Delta regain under the tariff. Congress still has not legislated weight-loss coverage, because the dementia label made a statute unnecessary for most voters over 60.

state.regulatory_posture: Federal, permissive on approvals, punitive on imports and now actively monitoring. FDA approved retatrutide 12 mg and the tirzepatide 60+ dementia extension. It issued the hypodipsia Drug Safety Communication and added anhedonia to the high-dose label. CMS audited AUD coding and recouped ~$310M. No state legislature acted on incretins, and Illinois's ban is still the only one.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: No weight-loss statute. Public coverage widened through labels: the dementia extension made Part D and Medicaid cover tirzepatide for most adults 60+ with BMI ≥27, and Medicaid AUD coverage keeps growing under existing rebate law. The NDAA FY2036 (signed Dec 2035) created a Metabolic Readiness authority for active duty. The 2027 tri-agency 30% guidance stands, and OPM's FEHB conditions continue.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: Deeper and more normal. Conditioned tracks hold 10.3M, and smart-bottle logs now record declared and undeclared holidays. Army MEDPROS records adherence for programme enrollees. Part D dementia-tier PA requires a DXA for women 65+ and annual renal and sodium labs. CMS audit pulls of telehealth records continue. Two state Medicaid programmes still condition coverage.
state.workforce_or_military: The NDAA FY2036 lets military treatment facilities prescribe incretins to soldiers who fail Army Body Composition Program standards. The programme enrolled ~140k by Dec 2036 across the services. The Army recruit oral pilot expanded to all initial-entry training sites. The 2035 VA/DoD guideline made oral semaglutide first-line for AUD. The Air Force allows aircrew on stable doses after a 90-day grounding and stability waiver. Police departments in Phoenix, Houston and Jacksonville fund officer programmes through DOJ COPS wellness grants. After the summer 2036 heat-injury reviews, TRADOC added hydration protocols for users. It did not pause the programme.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: The Section 232 100% tariff and Indian export-licence checks are unchanged. A WTO panel on Beijing's complaint is pending, with no ruling. Retatrutide 12 mg supply is capped by Lilly's US fill-finish until 2037, and DoD obtained a priority allocation under its Defense Production Act rated-order authority. That drew Senate questions about civilian waitlists. Smuggled API still feeds domestic re-filling.

events.event: VA and DoD publish a joint alcohol use disorder guideline naming oral semaglutide a first-line option alongside naltrexone and acamprosate; base-town bars around Fort Bragg and Killeen report sharp falls within months

Danish registry and VA cohort studies report that users on incretins continuously for five or more years drink less water, form more kidney stones and are hospitalised more often for heat illness; a Phoenix heat wave in August and an FDA safety communication in March 2036 follow

FDA extends tirzepatide's dementia-risk label to adults 60 and over with BMI 27 or higher, without heart disease; because it is not a weight-loss use, Part D and Medicaid must cover it, and Medicare incretin users reach 20.5 million by December 2036

The FY2036 defence bill lets military doctors prescribe incretins to service members who fail body-composition standards; 140,000 enroll in the first year under a no-holiday adherence rule, and Lilly gives DoD priority on high-dose retatrutide

FDA approves retatrutide 12 mg, about 29.5% average weight loss at 80 weeks and the first 'surgical-grade' pen; Lilly prices it at $1,499 list and $549 cash, allocates supply, and for the second straight year cuts no incretin price

Pew survey: 38% of incretin users took a planned 'drug holiday' last year and 22% lowered their own dose, mostly citing flatness; 64% of adults say being on the drug is 'just normal', and 'why are you off?' enters the vernacular

open_tensions: Medicare's new dementia label enrolled millions of adults over 60. That is the cohort most vulnerable to the hypodipsia signal, and it is now heading into five-year exposure, summer after summer. FDA answered with counselling rather than restriction.

The Army forbids drug holidays for soldiers in its readiness programme, even though flatness and heat illness argue for them. Commanders see adherence logs, and 11 of 63 summer heat injuries at two posts involved long-term users.

Prices stopped falling while the public share grew. Part D premiums rose 9%, retatrutide 12 mg is rationed by waitlist and a gray 'reta' market, and uninsured working-age Southerners remain outside every public route.

Holidays are now common practice, but conditioned tracks still penalise undeclared pauses. Employers, unions and platforms are fighting over whether feeling things for a week is a benefit, a breach or a feature to sell.

prose.headline: Eighty Million on It, Medicare Paying, Nobody Thirsty: How America's Drug Became Unremarkable and Its Holidays Didn't
prose.world_in_600_words:
At the end of 2036 about eighty-one million American adults take an incretin drug, a little under three in ten. Two in five have tried one. Nobody asks anymore why you are on it. People ask why you are off, and the answers have become a vocabulary of their own: between courses, priced out, pregnant, my pancreas, or the newest one, a holiday.

The biggest change happened without a vote. In November 2035 the FDA extended tirzepatide's dementia-risk label to adults over sixty with a BMI of 27 or more. The law still forbids Medicare to pay for weight loss, but dementia prevention is not weight loss, so Part D plans had to cover it and so did Medicaid. Within a year Medicare was paying for twenty and a half million users, and public programmes became the largest single payer of the class. In The Villages, Florida, the restaurants serve half plates, the potlucks serve tastings, and Sonoma growers are losing contracts because the people who drank their wine are now on the same weekly pen. Medicaid also kept absorbing alcohol-disorder patients under rules written for other purposes, and no state ever decided to pay for them.

Prices stopped falling. With older Americans enrolling by the million and Lilly unable to fill enough pens of its new high-dose retatrutide, neither company cut a price in 2035 or 2036. The Wegovy starting pill is still $149 through TrumpRx, and six million people still live on it indefinitely. Part D premiums rose nine percent. Retatrutide 12 mg took off about thirty percent of body weight in its trial, as much as surgery. It costs $549 in cash, and the waitlist is weeks long. The gray market fills the gap with 'reta' vials that the 2033 tariff has made expensive but not scarce.

The military made the drug part of readiness. The defence bill signed in December 2035 lets military doctors prescribe it to soldiers who fail the tape test, and the VA and Pentagon now list the alcohol pill as a first-line treatment. About 140,000 service members enrolled in the first year. Unlike civilians, they are forbidden to pause.

Pausing has become ordinary because the flatness is now a common complaint rather than a selling point. A federal analysis found dose-related loss of pleasure in about one in twenty low-dose users and one in eight on high-dose retatrutide, mostly reversible after a few weeks off. So people go off for a few weeks. They skip doses before weddings, Thanksgiving and anniversaries. Caterers ask about it on RSVP cards. Unions bargained over holiday quotas in the employer tracks, where an undeclared pause still drops a family's premium tier. Critics use 'flat' to describe a kind of album.

Then the long tail moved. Studies from Denmark and the VA found that people on these drugs continuously for five years or more drink less water than they need. They get more kidney stones and are hospitalised more often in heat. Nothing like this appeared in the trials. During the August 2035 Phoenix heat wave, emergency rooms noticed. The FDA told doctors to counsel scheduled drinking and check sodium in summer, and grocery chains built electrolyte bays. At Fort Moore and Fort Bragg, the summer's heat-casualty reviews found long-term users among the injured NCOs. The Army added a hydration protocol and kept the programme. Six million Americans have now passed five years of continuous use, and most of the next cohort to cross that line is old, covered and living in the Sun Belt.

The backlash of 2034 has thinned into separate complaints. Children aged six to eleven still grow half a centimetre a year more slowly on the drug, most of them on Medicaid. The Delta still calls the tariff a hunger tax.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Gloria Pruitt's water bottle chirps at 7:10, before the coffee. It is forty ounces, translucent green, a freebie from the Publix pharmacy counter the week the FDA letter came out. She drinks to the first line while Earl reads the paper aloud.

She takes the pen from the butter compartment, pinches her stomach and counts to ten. Tirzepatide, 5 mg, the dementia tier, $47 a month on her Part D plan. Her mother had forgotten Gloria's name by seventy-eight. The DXA in January said her hips were 'acceptable for now'.

Earl has been on the semaglutide pill since 2029 for his sugar, seven years, and he passed a stone in June. His bottle is blue. He forgets it in the golf cart.

Pickleball at nine, ninety minutes, three refills. At the Lake Sumter Landing café the menu has a 'half plate' column, and nobody at the table orders from the other one. Marjorie is off. Her granddaughter's wedding is Saturday, and she wants to taste the cake. Everyone nods. Nobody asks how many weeks.

At two her daughter Dana calls from Dayton. Her plant's plan allows two declared holidays a year, and she spent one in March. She sounds fine. She sounds the way she has sounded for three years.

At five-thirty they split a grouper sandwich. The bottle chirps. Earl says the Villages used to smell like fryer oil on Thursdays.

At nine Gloria checks the thermostat, then checks the bottle, then fills it for the nightstand.
